gaps.sentence: Hardly had we arrived ___ the storm broke.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly... when' is the fixed pair for one event interrupting another.

gaps.sentence: I can't afford a holiday this year; ___, I can't get the time off work.
gaps.explanation: 'Besides' adds a further, often decisive, reason in informal style.

gaps.sentence: He was warned repeatedly; ___, he ignored every safety rule.
gaps.explanation: He ignored the warnings despite receiving them: nevertheless marks that contrast.

gaps.sentence: ___ the roadworks, the coach still arrived ahead of schedule.
She is not only a gifted violinist ___ a composer of some note.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only A but also B' joins the two parallel noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: It sounds ___ the negotiations are close to a breakthrough.
gaps.explanation: 'It sounds as though...' reports an impression.

gaps.sentence: The course offers not only theory ___ hands-on fieldwork.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only... but also' is the fixed correlative pair.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.
